question: A 62-year-old female with a history of uncontrolled hypertension undergoes kidney transplantation. One month following surgery she has elevated serum blood urea nitrogen and creatinine and the patient complains of fever and arthralgia. Her medications include tacrolimus and prednisone. If the patient were experiencing acute, cell-mediated rejection, which of the following would you most expect to see upon biopsy of the transplanted kidney?

options.opa: Sloughing of proximal tubular epithelial cells
options.opb: Lymphocytic infiltrate of the tubules and interstitium
options.opc: Drug precipitation in the renal tubules
options.opd: Granular immunofluorescence around the glomerular basement membrane

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Acute, cell-mediated rejection -> Inflammatory response in the transplanted kidney -> Lymphocytic infiltrate of the tubules and interstitium -> 85% CHAIN: Tacrolimus and prednisone medications -> Immunosuppression -> Increased risk of rejection -> Acute, cell-mediated rejection -> Lymphocytic infiltrate of the tubules and interstitium -> 80% CHAIN: Elevated serum blood urea nitrogen and creatinine -> Impaired kidney function -> Possible rejection -> Acute, cell-mediated rejection -> Lymphocytic infiltrate of the tubules and interstitium -> 85%
enhanced_information: In acute, cell-mediated rejection following kidney transplantation, biopsy of the transplanted kidney would most likely show lymphocytic infiltrate of the tubules and interstitium. This is supported by the consensus that rejection involves an inflammatory response with lymphocytic infiltration, which is further confirmed by the retrieved evidence paths related to immunosuppression and inflammatory responses in the interstitium.
analysis: In the context of acute, cell-mediated rejection following kidney transplantation, the most likely finding upon biopsy of the transplanted kidney is a lymphocytic infiltrate of the tubules and interstitium. This aligns with the consensus that rejection involves an inflammatory response with lymphocytic infiltration. Sloughing of proximal tubular epithelial cells, drug precipitation in the renal tubules, granular immunofluorescence around the glomerular basement membrane, and crescent formation in Bowman’s space are not typical features of acute, cell-mediated rejection.
